absent: Charging, uncharging, high limit deferral, memory event delivery, and effective protection computation delegated to helpers outside these fragments.
Locking discipline and lifetime for peak observers, threshold sets, event subscriptions, writeback linkage, and per node vectors beyond member names.
Internal layout and update rules for usage counters, virtual memory statistics, pressure state, writeback domain, address space lists, and zone size tables.
Enabled build behavior for huge page charging, swap in charging, folio replacement, and folio migration.
Delivery mechanics for threshold notifications, out of memory notifications, pressure events, and file based event streams.
Computation of effective minimum and low values and interaction with parallel reclaimers having different targets.
Allocation and reuse of private identifiers and packing of identifiers for external reporting.
Per processor statistics aggregation and memory event tally retention across hotplug and teardown.

findings.text: The accounting group object starts with generic hierarchy linkage and a private durable identifier that remains valid after directory removal. Primary charge is tracked by one usage counter, while a second counter changes meaning with interface version, covering either swap alone or combined memory plus swap. Two observer lists for local peak notifications share one spin lock for mutation. Range enforcement is deferred to scheduled work. Additional always present state covers pressure feedback, a flag for group wide termination, file handles for event streams, centralized statistics plus per processor statistics kept on a separate cache line, tallies for memory events and local memory events, a socket pressure hint, and a trailing flexible array.

Several members exist only under build options. Compressed swap backing adds a limit and a flag controlling writeback and fallback on store failure. Writeback support adds a list, a domain object, and a small array of writeback records. One build option adds a per group list of address spaces. A wider legacy block adds separate kernel and network counters, per processor event storage, a soft limit, locking state for out of memory handling, a disable switch, a mutex guarding threshold arrays, two threshold sets for memory and for combined usage, a notification list, network accounting activation plus pressure level, a generic event subscription list with its own spin lock, and a tuning integer.
The charge coalescing granularity used by the accounting path is fixed at 64.

Low positions zero, one, and two of the per folio accounting word carry defined meanings. Position zero marks presence of a vector of per object extensions, and position one marks accounting as non slab kernel memory. Position two is reserved as first free value for extension flags. Two build dependent spellings exist for the allocation failure marker and for the first extension flag base, one reusing the vector marker and the free position, the other using position zero for both.

Extension flag space defines an allocation failure encoding that shares the lowest position, an unused placeholder occupying the first free position, and a next value marker at twice that base. A mask covering all defined extension flag positions is formed as one less than the next marker, allowing pointer bits to be isolated by clearing low positions.

A zero accounting word means no charge is present. A non zero word normally holds an object group pointer with low flag positions cleared, optionally combined with the kernel memory marker. When the vector indicator is set the word no longer holds a direct pointer and resolution helpers report absence. Slab folios never use the direct pointer path, and tail pages are excluded from page level checks. Kernel memory status is only meaningful when the vector indicator is clear.

The accounting word moves among a small set of encodings. Uncharged is zero. Charged without extensions is a pointer plus optional kernel marker. Vector mode is indicated by the lowest flag and requires different lookup. Allocation failure is encoded as the lowest flag alone without valid upper pointer bits. Helpers distinguish these states by testing the vector flag first, then masking low positions to recover the pointer.

Reading the group pointer stored inside an object group requires either read side critical section protection or ownership of the generic hierarchy lock. Several lookup and accounting paths enter a read side critical section internally before resolving the group from a folio, page, or address space owner, then release it before returning. The helper that pins a group from an object group retries when the subsystem reference attempt fails, ensuring a stable reference is returned.

Peak observer lists share one spin lock. Legacy threshold arrays are mutated under a dedicated mutex while readers use safe reclamation. Legacy event subscriptions have a separate spin lock. On narrow word machines an extra sequence lock member exists alongside the socket pressure hint. Out of memory coordination state in legacy mode is documented as guarded by a global out of memory lock.

Usage is observed through a single atomic observation of the primary counter. Protection queries return zero for minimum, low, and usage when the feature is unavailable. Targeted reclamation receives no protection, so queries against the reclaim root report zero minimum and low while still reporting usage. Otherwise the stored effective minimum and low values are returned. A group counts as unprotected when the feature is off, when it is the root, or when it equals the reclaim target. Below checks compare the effective threshold against current usage only when protected.

Resolution helpers map folios and pages to their owning groups. One helper extracts the object group by masking flag positions. Another maps that object group to the enclosing group or absence. Checked variants handle vector mode and tail pages by reporting absence instead of asserting. A pinning helper returns a referenced group suitable for use beyond the critical section. Kernel memory queries report whether the kernel marker is present.

Charging associates a folio with a group derived from an address space, while uncharging releases single folios or batches. When the feature is unavailable charging reports success immediately and uncharging does nothing. When available the work is delegated to out of scope implementations.

Reclaim vectors are selected per group and node. When the feature is off the node global vector is used. An absent group selects the root group. The per node structure is indexed by node number, and the vector back pointer to the node is repaired when nodes come online after group creation or after offline plus online cycles. Reverse mapping from vector to group reports absence when unavailable and otherwise uses container linkage, and per zone per list sizes are read with single atomic access. Folio based selection warns once when no group is found while the feature is enabled.

Root object groups are never reference counted and pinning them always succeeds. Non root object groups use a per processor reference that supports single and bulk acquisition plus single release. Memory groups tolerate absent handles, where pinning succeeds trivially and release does nothing. Present memory groups delegate to subsystem reference primitives, including an online variant. A container macro derives the enclosing group from a member counter address.

Identity helpers convert between subsystem state, sequence context, and group pointers, returning absence for absent input. Parent lookup follows the hierarchy link. Descendant testing treats equality as success and otherwise delegates to generic ancestry. Address space matching resolves the owner task group under protection and checks ancestry. Numeric identity comes from the group identifier, with zero for absent input, while a private short identifier returns zero when unavailable. Online status reports affirmative when unavailable and otherwise reflects subsystem state.

Root detection compares against the global root pointer, with object groups using a dedicated boolean marker. Availability is determined by whether the memory subsystem is enabled. Shrinker context counts as root when no group is attached or when the attached group is root. When unavailable the shift for identifier packing is zero and the root pointer is absent. Identifier lookup from an address space falls back to root when no owner group is found.

Statistic updates are ignored when unavailable. Page scoped updates resolve the folio group under protection before applying the delta. Folio event counting first checks for any charge, then resolves the group and forwards the tally. Address space scoped event counting and memory event notification resolve the owner group and forward when present. Over high handling checks a per task backlog counter and delegates only when non zero. The low level delta and event forwarders observed here have no effect.

Unavailable builds replace behavior with inert defaults. Group lookups yield absence, charge state and kernel markers report negative, and root and online checks report affirmative. Protection outputs are zero, below threshold checks report negative, and unprotected checks report affirmative. Charging reports success, huge page and swap in charging report success, uncharging and migration and replacement do nothing, statistic and event updates do nothing, and vector selection always returns the node global vector.

The accounting word can change asynchronously for slab objects, so checked lookup must use a single atomic read rather than plain access. Node structures may be missing or stale when nodes are hot added or cycled, requiring lazy repair of the vector back pointer on each mapping. Parallel reclaimers with different targets can observe inconsistent effective protections, so targeted reclamation explicitly drops protection to preserve the invariant. Deferred upper bound work must be triggered only when the per task backlog is non zero to avoid spurious wakeups.

Direct pointer extraction is only valid for non slab folios without vector mode and is guarded by debug checks. Kernel marker queries similarly require non tail pages and absence of vector mode. Folio to vector mapping warns when the lookup yields absence while accounting is active, indicating a missing association.
